frontMatter.value: Minimalism at any step: before writing code the request leaves open, climb the lazy-senior ladder (does it need to exist, is it already in the repo, does the stdlib or platform cover it, can it be one line) and build only on a measured need; subtract before you add; keep call chains flat; migrate every caller and delete the old API in one wave; mark each deliberate shortcut with a ponytail: comment naming its ceiling. Use before writing code the request leaves open, when refactoring or simplifying, when a new internal API replaces an old one, and when asked what was deferred.

passages.text: ponytail is the habit for the moment code the request leaves open is about to be written, a refactor or a simplification of code that works begun, a new internal API introduced while old callers remain, or the owner asks what was deferred, at whatever step the work is in, most often build; code the request plainly asks for does not load it. It writes no record of its own: a shortcut it takes is marked in the code and named in the build section of the change record. Where the ladder says reuse or skip, the change's acceptance still decides the scope, and tdd still decides the tests: a smaller implementation satisfies them too. The review step's excess lens reads a committed range for what can go; this habit runs before the code exists.
passages.reason: One opening paragraph in the habit's own voice: the situations the block's rows key it by, code the request leaves open and not code it plainly asks for, since QA runs loaded it ahead of its situation (J-60, the fourth family); that it writes no record of its own and the build section names a shortcut, that acceptance and tdd still bound a smaller implementation, and where the review step's excess lens stands beside it.
passages.gist: Opens the habit: code the request leaves open, bounded by acceptance
passages.ruling: The operator's card of 2026-10-15 on the QA series, "One fix job after the fifth family", with the delegation of 2026-10-16 whose words finalise the fix job's slices: a start or a habit loads only in the situation its row names, architecture-survey at an orientation and never as one where a change record exists, secrets only with a secret in reach and ponytail before code the request leaves open; a start is named in the record only when it ran; the survey never opens its report; a session with nothing to resume says so and asks for the request; diagnose ranks its hypotheses before the first probe and keeps them ranked; and ponytail builds only on a measured need and reads simplify.md before a refactor

passages.text: Build only on a need you measured. Where the first rung turns on a measurement, take it before building; where it shows no need, say so with the numbers and build nothing. A choice the owner leaves to you takes that answer; the owner, told the numbers, may still ask for the build.
passages.reason: The first rung builds only on a measured need, and a choice the owner leaves to the agent takes a measurement's answer of none, since a QA run built an index after measuring no need (J-60, the fifth family).

passages.text:
## Refactoring and deferrals

Replacing code that already works is a refactor, a scan by an index or a loop by a library call included: before its first edit, read [simplify.md](simplify.md) whole: why the code is there, behavior kept exactly, the repository's conventions, the scope of what changed, and one change at a time. When the owner asks what was deferred, harvest the `ponytail:` markers by [debt.md](debt.md).
passages.reason: code-simplification's selected passages and ponytail-debt's harvest live on simplify.md and debt.md, read only on their branch, so the body names each page and what it holds; replacing working code is a refactor that reads simplify.md whole first, since a QA run replaced a working scan with an index and left it unread (J-60, the fifth family).
passages.gist: A refactor, replacing working code included, reads simplify.md first
